data.title: Micron Stock Wobbles as Taiwan Workers Reject 68 Months' Pay, Demand Profit-Sharing
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) stock rose in premarket trading on Tuesday even though workers at the chipmaker's Taiwan facilities rejected a record compensation package and continued to push for a permanent share of the company's profits. The labor dispute comes as Micron benefits from strong demand for AI memory chips used in data centers. Taiwan is a critical manufacturing hub for Micron, with about 15,000 employees on the island.

The unions have pointed to compensation arrangements at South Korean memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) and SK Hynix (SKHY) as benchmarks. Micron workers are seeking a system that would allow employees to share more directly in the company's profitability during strong memory-market cycles.

Why Workers Are Pushing for Profit-Sharing

Micron recently announced fiscal 2026 rewards for its Taiwan employees equivalent to 35 to 68 months of pay. The package included an NT$1 million ($31,500) additional cash bonus for eligible employees who joined before August 29, 2025. Entry-level engineers were expected to receive average total rewards of about NT$3.4 million, including cash and equity.

However, Taiwan's Micron unions rejected the package, arguing that it does not address their broader demand for a permanent profit-sharing system. Specifically, the unions are seeking 15% of Micron's global operating profit to be allocated to employees.

Strike Risk Remains

No strike has been called, and there has been no reported impact on production so far. The dispute could become more significant if negotiations fail. The unions have said they could move toward a strike vote if Micron does not present a concrete proposal during mediation sessions scheduled for September 18 and 21.

Any disruption could raise concerns about supplies of DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which are increasingly important for AI infrastructure. It remains to be seen whether Micron can resolve the dispute without affecting production as demand for AI-related memory remains exceptionally strong.

data.title: HOOD, MSTR, COIN: Crypto Stocks Slide Ahead of Senate CLARITY Act Vote
data.description:
Cryptocurrency stocks Robinhood (HOOD), Coinbase (COIN), and Strategy (MSTR) fell in premarket trading Tuesday ahead of a congressional vote on the CLARITY Act on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC) was down nearly 2%, while Ethereum ($ETH-USD) fell 1.5%. Investors are also waiting for the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision, which could add to market volatility.

For context, the CLARITY Act aims to create a clearer regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies. The bill had previously faced delays over concerns about its safeguards against conflicts of interest and illicit finance.

Two Major Events Ahead for the Crypto Market

Investors are waiting for two key events in the next 24 hours. The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on Wednesday, which would lift its target range to 3.75%-4.00%.

Investors are also watching the Senate vote for clues about the future of digital asset rules. The vote could be an important test for the crypto market. If the bill fails to advance, investor sentiment could weaken, putting more pressure on digital assets. The Senate is set to vote on the CLARITY Act on Tuesday. The bill needs at least 60 votes to advance.

Recent weaker Bitcoin ETF inflows have added to the pressure on crypto stocks.

What the CLARITY Act Means for Crypto Companies

The CLARITY Act would aim to create clearer rules for cryptocurrency companies by defining how digital assets are regulated in the U.S. It could also clarify which regulators oversee different types of crypto assets and activities. This may give crypto companies more certainty as they build and expand their businesses.

It could help the crypto industry attract more institutional capital by giving asset managers, pension funds, and banks clearer rules for entering spot and derivatives markets. It could also encourage U.S. crypto companies to keep their projects and jobs in the country rather than moving offshore.

However, clearer rules could also raise costs for smaller startups. Companies may face higher legal, audit, and anti-money laundering compliance costs, along with stricter disclosure requirements.

data.title: Qualcomm Stock (QCOM) Falls as Rival MediaTek Beats It to First 2nm Smartphone Chip
data.description:
Shares in U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm (QCOM) edged lower to around $179 per share during Tuesday's pre-market session. This followed Taiwan-based smartphone chip rival MediaTek's launch of the Dimensity 9600 Pro. This is MediaTek's flagship smartphone chip, produced using the advanced 2nm process node. Chips made with this process contain billions more transistors. This makes devices with these chips faster, more powerful, and more energy-efficient. The rollout means MediaTek has beaten Qualcomm to the 2nm smartphone chip launch race.

For context, MediaTek is the world's largest smartphone chipmaker. According to Counterpoint Research, as of the first quarter of this year, MediaTek accounted for 32% of the global smartphone chipsets market. This is down from 38% a year ago. Qualcomm followed at 23%, also down from 27% in the same quarter last year.

data.title: AI Chip Startup Euclyd Sets Sights on Toppling Nvidia as It Raises €200M in New Funds
data.description:
Euclyd, a European artificial intelligence chip startup, has raised over €200 million in new funding to build its technology, aiming to rival the Graphics Processing Units built by semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA). The Dutch firm also named chip company ASML's (ASML) former chief executive Peter Wennink as its chairman.

No AI Constraints

The Series A financing was co-led by Samsung Electronics (SSNLF), Somerset Capital Partners, the EU's Scaleup Europe Fund and Innovation Industries.

Euclyd was founded in 2024 to develop AI chip technology to challenge traditional GPU-based architectures. The company claims its system could deliver up to 100 times higher power efficiency for AI inference compared to Nvidia's latest chips. However, its technology is yet to be fully adopted by the AI chip industry. 

Promotion

NVDS: built for a short position on NVDA

Unlike traditional GPUs that move data through memory, Euclyd's system claims to process data in multiple locations at once. This will reportedly help reduce energy use, cost, and the size of AI data centers. 

Euclyd has said that its long-term vision is Abundant Intelligence: a future in which advanced AI is no longer constrained by infrastructure cost, power availability, or geography.

"AI is becoming a foundation of economic growth, scientific discovery, and national competitiveness, but its potential will remain constrained unless we fundamentally change the infrastructure beneath it," said Bernardo Kastrup, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Euclyd. "This financing accelerates our mission to make intelligence abundant through greater efficiency, lower cost per token, and broader access to advanced AI."

Dede Goldschmidt, Senior Vice President of Samsung Electronics and Head of the Samsung Semiconductor Innovation Center, added: "The next phase of AI will be defined not only by model innovation, but also by the efficiency and scalability of its infrastructure. Euclyd combines an accomplished team with a differentiated vision addressing constraints in AI datacenters."

European Chips Face Barriers

Euclyd said that the new funds will expand its engineering organization, accelerate its silicon and systems roadmap, strengthen ecosystem partnerships, and prepare the company for commercial deployment across enterprise, sovereign, and hyperscale AI markets.

European AI chip startups are, however, facing several funding and market challenges despite growing global interest in artificial intelligence hardware. This situation is largely due to Europe having a less developed semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem than in regions like the U.S. and parts of Asia, where advanced chip production is more established. 

Additionally, the market is highly influenced by geopolitical factors. For example, the U.S. has tightened export controls on advanced AI chips and related technologies. As a result, this has encouraged European companies to develop their domestic technologies and reduce their reliance on foreign suppliers.

data.title: Memory Chip Stocks Micron, SanDisk, Western Digital, and SK Hynix Are Rebounding in Pre-Market Today. What's Driving the Recovery, Sept. 15?
data.description:
Memory stocks Micron Technology (MU), SanDisk (SNDK), Western Digital (WDC), and SK Hynix (SKHY) are rebounding after Monday's sell-off. The recovery comes as Citi forecasts a widening memory shortage through 2031, while recent comments from AI industry leaders continue to point to strong demand for computing infrastructure despite calls to slow AI development.

The four stocks were hit hard Monday after AI industry leaders called for a slower pace of development. Investors are now focusing on the supply-demand outlook for memory chips rather than the AI slowdown debate.

Citi Sees Memory Shortages Getting Worse

Citi expects the memory market to remain undersupplied as AI workloads continue to expand. It named Samsung Electronics (SKHY), SK Hynix, Micron, SanDisk, and Kioxia among its top memory picks.

Promotion

Discover why XOVR identified Kalshi as an attractive private investment opportunity.

The bank said that continual learning could become an important part of AI development over the next five years. This could increase the need for HBM used in AI systems. It could also raise demand for enterprise SSDs as AI systems store more learned data.

Citi expects HBM bit demand to jump 62% year-over-year to 75.2 billion gigabits in 2027. It sees another 69% increase to 127 billion gigabits in 2028.

The supply picture is even tighter for DRAM. Citi expects global DRAM demand to rise 30% in 2027 and 35% in 2028. Supply is expected to grow only 19% and 22%, respectively. That would leave the DRAM supply-demand balance at deficits of 8.7% in 2027 and 9.7% in 2028.

NAND is also expected to remain tight. Citi sees demand rising 29% in 2027 and 33% in 2028, compared with supply growth of 21% and 25%.

AI Demand Concerns Are Easing

Investors are also getting more reassurance that Monday's AI fears do not reflect an actual collapse in spending. President Donald Trump defended continued AI development on Monday, saying the U.S. needs to keep advancing the technology while maintaining safeguards.

Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang also said the AI race should continue. His comments are relevant for memory stocks because high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is widely used in advanced AI accelerators.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan offered another sign of continued demand. He said the company's AI revenue forecasts remain intact. Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue of $21.7 billion in fiscal Q4, up 236% year-over-year. Its fiscal 2027 forecast stands at about $115 billion.

The comments do not rule out a slowdown in AI spending. They suggest that demand for AI computing remains strong for now.

Micron Earnings Could Be the Next Test for the Memory Rally

Micron also has a major near-term event that could help investors judge whether the memory boom remains intact. The company is scheduled to report fiscal fourth-quarter results on September 30. Wall Street expects about $31.14 in EPS and $50.41 billion in revenue, according to current estimates.

The company's Taiwan operations are also in focus. A union representing Micron workers warned Tuesday that it could move toward a strike vote if negotiations over profit sharing do not make progress. No strike has been called, and Reuters said there has been no production impact so far.

However, the dispute adds another supply-related variable for investors. Taiwan is an important production base for Micron's DRAM and HBM chips. Any prolonged disruption could further tighten an already constrained market.

According to the TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, Micron, SanDisk, and SK Hynix have Strong Buy ratings, while Western Digital has a Moderate Buy rating. Micron has the highest upside at 69.25%, followed by Western Digital at 59.49%, SK Hynix at 33.62%, and SanDisk at 40.63%.

data.title: Why Is Oracle Stock Falling in Pre-Market Today, Sept. 15?
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) stock is down by 1.24% in premarket trading today. The company has reportedly started another round of job cuts as it continues to spend heavily on AI infrastructure. Business Insider reported that the layoffs were expected to start Monday, citing affected employees and an internal notification email. Workers reportedly began receiving notices that their positions were being eliminated as part of a broader organizational change.

What Oracle Told Employees in Its Latest Layoff Email

"After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organisational change. As a result, today is your last working day," the notice said, according to a copy reviewed by Business Insider.

Reports began surfacing on social media early Monday that some Oracle employees were unable to access company systems, including email and Slack. For many workers, the loss of access appeared to signal that their jobs had been cut.

Promotion

Several former Oracle employees also shared details in a LinkedIn thread. They said layoff notices were not sent to their personal email accounts, leaving some workers unsure about their status. Some had to contact their managers, while others had already been told that their roles were at risk.

Under the severance plan, affected employees were reportedly offered four weeks of base salary, plus one additional week for each year they had worked at Oracle.

Another Round of Layoffs

The latest layoffs follow job cuts Oracle made earlier this year. The company's workforce fell by about 21,000 employees, or 13%, during the fiscal year ended May 31, according to a recent filing.

Oracle's latest quarterly SEC filing shows that the company is increasing its 2026 restructuring budget by another $700 million. Before the end of the quarter, Oracle had expected restructuring costs of up to $2.1 billion, mainly related to employee severance, contract termination fees, and other exit costs.

The higher restructuring budget comes as Oracle reported $19.3 billion in revenue for Q1 FY27, which ended August 31. The results show strong growth as Oracle continues to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. However, the company is also cutting jobs and raising spending on restructuring as it adjusts its workforce and business costs.
